correctness.rationale: Exact scope p,q>=2, named levels, reflexive transitive plus both forth conditions. Reconstructed normal form from the original implications; dual top-class forcing, predecessor-closed source ideals, and all mixed two-step transitivity cases checked. Isomorphisms split as S_p×S_q; the source ideals and preorder restrictions are complete equivariant invariants. Automorphism group is the corresponding product of stabilizers. Orbit formula follows by summing independent marked-ideal orbits. Greatest-class removal proves b_n/d_n prefix sums and direct Burnside proves c_n. Original-axiom exhaustive C checker yields 89/38 at (2,2) and 762/135 at (2,3)/(3,2); normal-form uniqueness and Burnside give 5922/452 at (3,3), while canonical representatives were computed directly through (3,2). Finite checks are supplementary; infinite assertions follow from structural proof.

originality.rationale: An accessible earlier labelled top-class classification for the exact same family was found and treated as covering the entire normal-form premise and labelled counts, so neither is claimed new. What remains is an explicit isomorphism classification by automorphism-orbits of admissible marked ideals, an exact stabilizer-product formula, and a universal two-parameter unlabelled count with marked-ideal and top-class recurrences. Direct searches of existing research results and primary full-text sources did not find these orbit statements. Residual unindexed-equivalence risk is recorded; a literature search is not proof of uniqueness.
residual_risks: Prior mathematical normal form is a decisive overlap for labelled results; the genuinely new scope must remain restricted to isomorphism classes, stabilizers and orbit-count formula.
An equivalent unlabelled count may exist under two-colored finite-topology, weighted-poset, or modal-frame terminology absent from indexing.
Not every conceivable secondary paper was available/inspected; independently verify novelty before publication.

value.rationale: A natural finite-model-theory invariant is the number of genuinely different finite semantics after renaming worlds, rather than labels. For a whole two-parameter infinite family, the work classifies each isomorphism type via automorphism-orbits of ideals and determines stabilizers and exact unlabelled counts. Marked-ideal orbit statistics are not recoverable by replacing factorials or just dividing labelled counts (89 labelled versus 38 unlabelled at 2+2); they encode nonfree actions. The result is a complete, mathematically motivated isomorphism classification, though not a general decidability theorem.
